high.title: Finance Minister Purbaya Promises No Tax Rate Hikes, But Will Pursue Tax Evaders
high.summary: Indonesian Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa confirmed the government will not raise tax rates despite efforts to boost state revenue. Instead, the government will aggressively pursue tax leakages, manipulation, and non-compliant taxpayers, including following up on public reports of companies avoiding tax obligations. This signals a shift toward stricter tax enforcement rather than rate increases, which is relevant for businesses operating in Indonesia.

high.title: Fuel Prices at BP Gas Stations Drop Starting August 1
high.summary: BP Indonesia has cut prices on gasoline products effective August 1, 2026, with BP 92 dropping from Rp 16,670 to Rp 16,130 per liter and BP Ultimate falling from Rp 17,240 to Rp 16,760 per liter. However, BP Ultimate Diesel rose from Rp 21,340 to Rp 21,910 per liter. These fuel price movements follow similar cuts by Pertamina and are significant for inflation expectations, logistics costs, and consumer spending in Indonesia.

high.title: Finance Minister Purbaya Promises No Tax Rate Hikes But Will Pursue Tax Evaders
high.summary: Indonesian Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa has confirmed the government will not raise tax rates while still aiming to boost state revenues. The strategy focuses on optimizing tax collection, closing revenue leakages, and actively pursuing companies suspected of tax manipulation or non-compliance. This signals a more aggressive enforcement stance from the tax authority without imposing additional burdens on compliant taxpayers, which is relevant for businesses operating in Indonesia.

high.title: BP Fuel Station Cuts Gasoline Prices, Raises Diesel Prices Effective August 1
high.summary: BP Indonesia has revised its fuel prices starting August 1, 2026, cutting BP 92 from IDR 16,670 to IDR 16,130 per liter and BP Ultimate from IDR 17,240 to IDR 16,760 per liter. However, BP Ultimate Diesel prices rose from IDR 21,340 to IDR 21,910 per liter. These price changes affect transportation and logistics costs across industries and are relevant to consumers and businesses reliant on fuel.

high.title: JCI Gains Slightly This Week, Daily Transaction Value Drops Sharply
high.summary: The Jakarta Composite Index (JCI) gained 0.64% for the week of July 27-31, 2026, closing at 6,236.126 with BEI market capitalization rising 0.48% to IDR 10,923 trillion. However, average daily transaction value fell sharply by 21.86% to IDR 15.44 trillion from IDR 19.76 trillion the prior week, signaling reduced market participation and liquidity concerns for investors.

high.title: JCI Closes Strong in Green Zone at Level 6,200s
high.summary: The JCI closed up 49.76 points (0.80%) at 6,236.12 on Friday, July 31, 2026, remaining consistently in positive territory throughout the session. Transaction volume reached 32.45 billion shares with a turnover of IDR 18.25 trillion across 1.95 million transactions, reflecting healthy end-of-week trading activity.

medium.title: Drivers Report No Engine Problems After Using B50 Biodiesel Blend at Gas Stations
medium.summary: Indonesia's B50 biodiesel mandate, which blends 50% palm oil into diesel fuel, officially launched on July 1, 2026, and early user reports indicate no significant engine performance issues. This is relevant for investors in Indonesia's palm oil sector, as the B50 policy is a key demand driver for crude palm oil (CPO). Continued positive reception could support sustained domestic CPO consumption and bolster the earnings outlook for palm oil producers.

medium.title: BGN Prioritizes Local Rice for School Meal Program (MBG), Bulog Supply Serves as Reserve
medium.summary: The National Nutrition Agency (BGN) has confirmed it will prioritize local food sources, including local rice, for the Free Nutritious Meal (MBG) program to strengthen regional economies and empower local farmers and SMEs. State logistics firm Bulog's role is limited to acting as a buffer supply when local sources are insufficient or price volatility occurs. This policy has implications for agricultural supply chains, UMKM businesses, and Bulog's commercial role in the national food distribution ecosystem.

medium.title: B50 Biodiesel (50% Palm Oil Blend) Shows No Engine Problems According to Early Users
medium.summary: Indonesia's B50 biodiesel mandate, which blends 50% palm oil into diesel fuel, officially took effect on July 1, 2026, and early user feedback suggests no significant engine issues. A truck driver in North Sumatra reported smooth engine performance after switching to B50, offering positive signals for the policy's rollout. This is significant for Indonesia's palm oil industry and energy sector investors, as B50 implementation directly impacts domestic palm oil demand.

medium.title: Allo Bank Posts Net Profit of IDR 130 Billion in Q2 2026, Up 14% YoY
medium.summary: PT Allo Bank Indonesia Tbk (BBHI) reported a net profit of IDR 130 billion in Q2 2026, growing 14% year-on-year from IDR 114 billion in the same period last year, supported by a 21% YoY rise in operating income to IDR 533 billion. Fee-based income surged 71% YoY to IDR 140 billion, highlighting strong diversification of revenue streams despite challenging macroeconomic conditions.

medium.title: RAJA's Net Profit Surges 88% to IDR 521 Billion in H1 2026
medium.summary: PT Rukun Raharja Tbk (RAJA) recorded revenue of USD 131.2 million (approx. IDR 2.36 trillion) in H1 2026, up 3% YoY, driven by the full contribution of its Sengkang Gas Compressor project which offset declining gas sales from pipeline disruptions in Sumatra. Net profit jumped 88% to USD 28.9 million (approx. IDR 521.82 billion), making it a standout performer in the energy sector for investors to watch.
